en.title: Backspace String Compare
en.description: Given two strings consisting only of lowercase English letters and `#`. `#` is a backspace that deletes the single character immediately before it in the current string; if the string is empty at that moment, it has no effect. Determine whether the two strings are equal after each is processed; output 1 if they are equal, otherwise output 0.
en.input: Two lines with the non-empty strings s1 and s2. Complete original constraints: 1≤|s1|,|s2|≤200000; characters are only lowercase English letters or `#`. The ranges come from the complete raw of the fixed submission; the `1 5` in the compiled MDX is a corrupted fragment. The two-line standard input/output is this site's wrapper.
en.output: Output 1 if they are equal, otherwise output 0.
en.explanation: A backspace on an empty string does nothing; all other rules follow the original definition. You can scan from right to left while counting characters to skip, or use a stack.
hints: When scanning from right to left, increase the skip count whenever you meet #; a normal character is skipped if the skip count is positive, otherwise it takes part in the comparison.
